Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Planning Commission Members will be participating via
teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
825 9363 2552 Passcode: 308499. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 825 9363 2552 Passcode: 308499.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 825 9363
2552 Passcode: 308499.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, DECEMBER 7, 2020

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR CARMAN at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CARMAN led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang

  Staff Members Present:  David Wahba, Community Development and Public Works Director
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Cameron Hall, Code Compliance Officer
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  Don Davis, City Attorney

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, OCTOBER 5, 2020

  VICE CHAIR EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 5, 2020.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the Planning
  Commission will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  VICE CHAIR EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVED ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  B.  2020 ANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT

  The Planning Commissioners agreed to move Item 5B to the end of the meeting.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  FENCE REGULATION STUDY SESSION

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation with the current code sections related to
  fences and staff’s recommendations.

  Sections 17.06.350 – Fences, hedges and walls “H” overlay district and 17.06.360 – Fences, walls,
  hedges, structures and similar landscape features in front yards and side yards abutting a street.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that currently front yard fences, hedges, and walls are limited
  to 24” except in the “H” overlay districts, where a standard three-rail 42” height fence is allowed.

  •  Staff is recommending that the allowance for a standard three-rail fence in the front yard, be
  extended to all residential districts in the City, as the three-rail fence is emblematic of the City’s
  character. In addition, staff is recommending that the 24” height limit for other fences, walls,
  and hedges, be allowed to extend up to 42”.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  1
MINUTES, DECEMBER 7, 2020
   COMMISSIONER SCOTT commented that in some neighborhoods three-rail fence would be out
  of character.

  Director Wahba stated that although, they do look out of character, there are some neighborhoods
  that have both fence heights throughout their neighborhoods.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Planning Manger Naughton stated
  that the reason for implementing a 42” fence height is due to requests from property owners
  pertaining to both topography and aesthetics.

  Section 17.06.370.A – Fences, hedges and walls-side and rear yard setbacks, developable areas.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that this section pertains to fencing in the side yard that face
  the street. Fencing must maintain the same required setback from the street side property line as
  required for the main building.

  •  Staff recommends that, for solid fencing, that the setback be a minimum of 2’ or possibly 18”
  at a minimum for the purposes of providing landscaping between the fence and the sidewalk,
  where a public sidewalk is present;

  •  In the case of a private street, the minimum setback from the pavement should be at least 5’.
  Where no sidewalk exists and the public right of way provides for at least 5’ of un-paved area
  or more, than the fence may be placed on the property line;

  •  Under a Minor Deviation application, there could be exceptions included for substandard width
  lots, and lots where existing residences are less than 10’ from edge of pavement, on a street-
  facing sideyard to further reduce the above-stated setback requirements;

  •  Open fences should still be allowed to be placed on the property lines but should be reduced
  from 90% open to 50% or possibly less. 90% open is only achieved by using chain link. Chain
  link fencing should be explicitly prohibited in side and rear setbacks.

  Director Wahba stated that the last recommendation regarding chain link fences is only for side
  and rear yards facing the street and this is only for clarification of this code section.

  In response to a question by CHAIR CARMAN regarding solid fencing, Director Wahba explained
  that the 2’ or 18” setback would be landscaped area and would serve as a “buffer” between the
  sidewalk and the fence. COMMISSIONER SCOTT suggested allowing a minimum of 5’ from the
  house to the solid fence.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he is in favor of staff’s recommendation regarding private
  streets.

  Section 17.06.370.B – Fences, hedges and walls-side and rear yard setbacks, developable areas.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff received correspondence from a resident of the
  Rollingwood neighborhood regarding this code section. The current code states that if there is a
  grade difference greater than 36” between two adjoining lots then no fencing or wall should extend
  more than 42” above the height of the upper building pad. Any fencing over 42” above the height
  of the building pad shall be open by at least 90%.

  •  Staff recommends that this section be clarified to be specific to fences on top of retaining walls,
  and that a 6’ high solid fence or wall be permitted on a side property line, regardless of grade
  separation.

  Director Wahba stated that typically the neighbor on the downhill grade is concerned with privacy
  from the above grade property

  In response to a comment by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  language can be added about nonconforming setbacks.

  Section 17.06.380 – Retaining walls.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that currently the maximum is 5’ and staff is not recommending
  that this be changed. However, currently a fence is not allowed to be placed above a retaining wall.
  In addition, when there is a situation where more than one retaining wall is needed or fence used
  on a slope, a minimum horizontal between the retaining wall and the fence that is equal to the
  height of the tallest wall and/or fence.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  2
MINUTES, DECEMBER 7, 2020
   •  Staff recommends that the horizontal separation be reduced to two feet, for purposes of
  providing landscaping between walls; this will ensure that there is not large, monolith walls built
  in the residential districts, while still providing articulation, by stepping back the series of walls
  and/or fences. A 42” high open fence/railing per building code will still be allowed to be placed
  on top of a retaining wall where a drop greater than 30” exists. Staff is also seeking direction
  as to whether a solid railing up to 42” high, or something partially open should be permitted in
  this section.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the materials of the retaining wall and fence be the same. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that they could be the same material.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there is any concern with having a large continuous wall. Director
  Wahba stated that the intent is that there will be landscaping in between to prevent this.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he is in favor of staff’s recommendation. In certain instances,
  and by Variance and consent of the downhill property owner, he has no issue with allowing a 6’
  fence on top of a 5’ retaining wall.

  Section 17.06.430 – Solid fencing-Landscaping required.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that this process requires Neighborhood Compatibility review
  for approval.

  •  Staff recommends simplifying this process, by creating an administrative avenue for approval.

  Section 17.40.040 – Design

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that any parcel of land that is used for off-street parking
  requires Planning Commission review.

  •  Staff recommends simplifying this process, by creating an administrative avenue for approval.
  Staff would also appreciate the Commission’s input on the creation of an administrative avenue
  for allowing alternative fence/wall heights for non-residential uses that are adjacent to
  residential uses, such as the Cal Water facility at the corner of Montecillo Drive and Encanto
  Drive.

  Director Wahba added that cases can come before the Commission, similar to the Special Use
  Permit process which is in place for tennis court / sport court fencing.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that an 8’ high block wall around the Cal Water facility would be
  a good idea for the community and for Cal Water.

  Section 17.66.100 – Minor Deviations

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that there are two Minor Deviations that deal with fences. (4)
  A Minor Deviation to allow an increase of not more than 10% of permitted height of the fence or
  wall with the exception of fenced recreational enclosures, which requires a Special Use Permit
  SUP application. (9) The permitted height of solid material fencing allowed in the rear and side
  yard setbacks where there is a grade differential of more than thirty-six inches between adjoining
  lots in the residential zones.

  •  Staff recommends that Minor Deviation #4 be modified as noted in italics above, and that Minor
  Deviation #9 be eliminated from the code, as staff would like to propose to modify the previous
  section (RHEMC Section 17.06.370.B), which addresses fencing height in grade differential
  scenarios.

  Tom Judge, Resident, stated that fences are being installed that are not complying with the code.
  He also expressed his concern with privacy/view issues and enforcement measures. Mr. Judge
  stated that he will provide his comments to Ms. Naughton.

  Additional visual aids will be brought back to the Planning Commission for review, to help assist in
  the discussion regarding these Code sections, at a future meeting.

  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-20-18 (MODIFICATION); ADDRESS: 19
  DAPPLEGRAY LANE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: MS. SHEELA DERANIYAGALA;
  A request to Modify approvals granted by the Planning Commission on March 4, 2019, which
  included a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for a one-story addition and deck to an
  existing one-story, single family residence; a Minor Deviation for the one-story addition to be built
  along the existing building line that encroaches into the legal nonconforming sideyard setback; and
  a Grading Permit for removal of the existing tennis court and related facilities. The applicant

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  3
MINUTES, DECEMBER 7, 2020
   requests to modify the Minor Deviation approval with a four (4) foot extension of the rear covered
  deck, which would maintain a 4’-11” nonconforming sideyard setback, and modification of the
  Grading Permit approval, by reduction of the grading involved with the tennis court and related
  facilities removal.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided background on this project and stated that this item was last
  brought before the Planning Commission at the August meeting. The revised addition will be the
  same size, the new deck is approximately 377 sq. ft., the stairs from the deck were reconfigured
  to come off the south end. When this case was last brought to the Planning Commission, the most
  concerning issues were on the northern elevation of the covered deck area due to privacy
  concerns. The applicant had proposed a live wall, which was determined to be insufficient in
  addressing the privacy issue. The Planning Commission requested that the applicant bring back
  alternative solutions.

  Planning Manager Naughton added that another issue was in relation to the southerly property
  line. Originally, the property owner had proposed to remove the tennis court that exists on the
  property and bring the grading down to match that of the property line of the adjacent neighbor.
  However, the grading could not be achieved; the applicant has proposed to retain the existing
  retaining wall.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided photographs of the louvre privacy screens on the northerly
  side of the property and noted that this was installed in violation of the stop work order issued by
  the City. A site plan showing the proposed retaining wall on the southerly side of the property was
  also presented.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff can only support the deck extension if the northern
  elevation includes a solid wall using materials that match the primary residence and that it extend
  from plate line to finished floor. Without this solid wall, staff would recommend that the deck be
  built according to the original approval.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
  modifications to PA-20-18, subject to the conditions as outlined in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked why staff could not support approval of the louvres, assuming
  they are fixed and allow no sight visibility to the neighbor to the north. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that the louvres appear to be operable and privacy would be dependent on whether they
  are opened or closed. COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if staff could support the louvres if they
  were fixed to allow no visibility. Planning Manager Naughton stated yes, as long as the applicant’s
  plans could show that the louvres will be fixed.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  any mechanical equipment is required to be setback 10 ft. from the property line; in this case, it will
  need to be confirmed that the air conditioning unit that is proposed is not encroaching into the 10
  ft.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed his concern with the applicant’s contempt for the process.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired about the fines and how they are collected. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that the fines are from $100 - $500 and added that building without
  permits also will incur double permit fees when this project goes back to building and safety.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired if we are at a point where other legal action should be
  taken towards this applicant, since there seems to be a disregard to the stop work orders. Attorney
  Davis stated that it could be something to consider on some of the discretionary items. There will
  be significant penalties, as has been discussed.

  Attorney Davis stated that he would like to address the Variance issue for this project. When
  discussion arose regarding the fencing code, there was discussion of whether or not there was a
  Variance. He noted to staff, that placing the fence on top of the retaining wall would be a violation
  of the code (Section 17.06.380). Variances are only for very unique situations and if the code does
  not work, a Variance could not apply.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the inaccessibility for demolition and narrow lot special
  circumstance for Variance findings. Attorney Davis stated that for the fence on top of the retaining
  wall, a Variance would not be applicable. Planning Manager Naughton added that the tennis court
  can still be removed, however, is would be more expensive, since the removal of the demolished
  material will need to be removed manually due to the inaccessibility to the rear of the property by
  heavy equipment.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  4
MINUTES, DECEMBER 7, 2020
   COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there was a position taken by the neighbor to the north regarding
  the louvres that were installed. Planning Manager Naughton stated that in conversations with the
  property owner, the feeling was that the louvres were inadequate to address privacy concerns.

  Ms. Deraniyagala, Property Owner, 19 Dapplegray Lane, stated that there were privacy issues
  with 21 Dapplegray Lane. The deck was approved and it was built 4 ft. over what was approved,
  but stated that coming from her master bedroom, you can see toward the windows at 21
  Dapplegray Lane, and stated that there is no difference on visibility with the 4 ft. extension. The
  reason that the louvres were installed, is to show that they could provide privacy for both properties.

  Ms. Deraniyalaga stated that there have been a lot of complaints since starting the project and
  stated that people are harassing her workers and come onto her property without masks.

  Ms. Deraniyalaga stated that the photographs showing that steps are being constructed behind
  her bedroom window are actually planters. She added that there was a call to code compliance
  regarding illegal activity, however, it was just the gardener removing the debris from her property.

  Kirk Retz, 18 Dapplegray Lane, stated that on the fencing issue on the south side, building a 6 ft.
  fence on top of the retaining wall would provide a solution for the privacy issue on that side. Mr.
  Retz expressed his concern for the disregard to the stop work orders that were issued. Mr. Retz
  also expressed his concern with the foundation for a solid wall as recommended for the north side
  of the property.

  Lisa Johnson, 17 Dapplegray Lane, stated that there is a severe slope in the rear of her property.
  She stated that in speaking with Ms. Deraniyalaga, they both would like privacy and if a fence is
  installed on the property line, then at the end of the tennis court the top of the fence will be level
  with the retaining wall. Not only privacy but also safety should be considered in this discussion and
  in this case, the south side property owners agree. Ms. Johnson stated that this is trying to solve
  the problem of a tennis court that should not have been built in the first place.

  Sam Silva, Contractor of 19 Dapplegray Lane, stated that regarding the question about the
  foundation of the deck, it is able to withstand a two-story building if need be. He stated that per the
  request of the neighbor at 21 Dapplegray, he was asked to install a mock-up of the louvres and
  that is what was installed. The city came out to issue a citation, however, the louvres are not bolted
  to the building. If the louvres are approved, then they will be installed permanently in their place.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Mr. Silva stated that the louvres are not
  operable.

  Grant Mogford, 21 Dapplegray Lane, stated that Mr. Silva was supposed to send plans to him back
  in October, but they have not been received. In regards to the louvres that were installed, from his
  dressing room you can see through the louvres down onto the deck and assumes that from the
  deck, someone could see into his dressing room. The louvres need to be tilted to the opposite
  direction and also added that the wood is already warping. He stated that he does not think that
  the louvres will address the privacy issues.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about Mr. Mogford’s position on the solid wall extension.
  Mr. Mogford stated that the solid wall would resolve the privacy issue or he would like to go back
  to the original plan.
